title: There Is / There Are
description: Say what exists in a room or neighborhood.
objectives: Say what exists in a room or neighborhood.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to say what exists in a room or neighborhood. The central language is there is for singular and there are for plural. It belongs to the practical context of home & around town. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: there is for singular and there are for plural

blocks.english: There is a table by the window.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the there is / there are exchange.

blocks.english: There are three chairs in the kitchen.
blocks.explanation: This there is / there are model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the there is / there are exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “There is a table by the window.” and “There are three chairs in the kitchen.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: there is for singular and there are for plural.

items: Communicative goal: Say what exists in a room or neighborhood.
Core pattern: there is for singular and there are for plural.
Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
